paper: Xiao, Cui, Mai, Xu, Li. Short Interest Trend Prediction with Large Language Models. ICIAI 2024. doi:10.1145/3655497.3655500

dataset_sources.news_titles: Kaggle dataset miguelaenlle/massive-stock-news-analysis-db-for-nlpbacktests ('Daily Financial News for 6000+ Stocks', CC0), file analyst_ratings_processed.csv (Benzinga headlines)
dataset_sources.label_set_A: FINRA Reg SHO Daily Short Sale Volume files, https://cdn.finra.org/equity/regsho/daily/ (FNSQ, FNYX, FNQC, FNRA), 2009-08-03 to 2020-07-15
dataset_sources.label_set_B: FINRA consolidated short interest, https://cdn.finra.org/equity/otcmarket/biweekly/, settlement dates 2017-12-29 to 2020-08-31, exchange-listed only

preprocessing: ASCII-only titles; 1-50 tokens (google/flan-t5-base tokenizer); exact duplicate (title, ticker, date) rows removed; news date = US/Eastern calendar date; company name = FINRA issue name if available, else ticker

regsho_volume.definition: A: paper-faithful; sign of change in FINRA daily short-sale VOLUME (t+1 vs t-1)

short_interest.definition: B: true short interest; sign of change between FINRA bi-monthly short-interest reports

split: stratified 80/20 train/test (sklearn train_test_split, random_state=42); evaluation sample = stratified 500 titles from the test split (random_state=42), identical across shot settings

prompt.template:
Read the news title below and determine how the short interest of {company} changes.

{title}

OPTIONS:
1. increase
2. decrease

ANSWER:
prompt.demonstrations: drawn at random from the training split without replacement, fixed per test title (numpy seed 42*1000003 + index); each = template + ' <gold label>'; joined with blank lines

inference.parsing: earliest of 'increase', 'decrease', '1.', '2.' in the lowercased output; none found = invalid (counted as wrong)

metrics: sklearn f1_score with labels=[increase, decrease]: per-class F1, support-weighted F1, macro F1; 95% CI = 2000 bootstrap resamples of the 500 titles

baselines.majority: always predict the training majority class ('increase')
baselines.random: predict 'increase' with probability = training share of 'increase' (numpy seed 42)
baselines.tfidf_logreg: TfidfVectorizer(ngram_range=(1,2), min_df=3, max_features=500000, sublinear_tf=True) + LogisticRegression(C=1, class_weight='balanced', solver='liblinear'), titles only
